Just finished the main storyline and a couple of side missions and challenge tombs, and I have to say that this is one of the best games I have ever played. I loved the story line and the game really shines when it comes to challenge tombs. This game is taken place in a jungle in the amazon and I prefer this environment rather than the cold siberia in the previous game Rise of the Tomb Raider. There are plenty of stuff to do in this game. I have played around 18 hours by now and I have completed more or less 70% of the game.

I'm running this game on a crappy computer therefore I have experienced plenty of lag when it comes to some cutscenes and special effects. I have been using 8 GB of RAM and this game has always used up the majority of that. I would recommend 16 GB of RAM to avoid unnessecary lag. Otherwise I think a GTX 960 as a graphics card is fine and an Intel Core i5 works alright when it comes to CPU:s.

Good luck fellow tomb raiders and have a great time playing this game!

Frustrating game. I liked the previous two games in the series but this has far too many cut-scenes that break up the rhythm for a story that doesn't really hit the mark. The gameplay can be fun, as it was in the earlier episodes but unfortunately there are too many automated mechanics where you have to wait for Lara to finish doing or saying something before having any control. I'm still trying to finish it but I get bored after 15 minutes. Maybe I'm getting old.

The graphics are amazing, side missions are fun, and I enjoyed every minute of it.

Despite looking gorgeously lush, with beautiful cinematography during cutscenes, Shadows is unfortunately underbaked. The platforming controls respond poorly, combat is tedious and punishes stealth, environmental lighting and animations break frequently, and many puzzles are poorly designed and require the player to mash the interact key on every rock Monkey Island style. Too often I've had to watch a gameplay video to figure out which rocky ledge on a wall is climbable and which one is just set dressing. It's clear that whoever was in charge of this game simply rehashed the old engine and phoned it in. An unfortunate waste of money.

The bad - occasional crashes, frustrating seem to be related to direct x 12 and high speed refresh rate and playing full screen bugs - the only way around one of these is when you find one turn of direct x 12 cap your frame rate at 60 fps and go from full screen to windowed even then expect animations to be a bit "janky".

This is the best Tomb Raider game to date. Apart from graphics that still easily rival ours in 2024, the experience of delving into the dark Chilean jungles is deeply atmospheric and keeps you playing just for the thrill of discovery. While the dungeon (sorry, tomb) puzzles are game'ified with ordered debris and convenient dilapidated ruins for climbing, it still rarely detracts from the experience. Some have reported the paths to be hard to spot but I've had few issues even with hints turned off. The story is the usual world-spanning doomsday that Lara has to avert from the previous few games, with the characters a bit tame despite the rough setting seeping with Aztec death and ritualism. Nonetheless there is a drop of ambiguity in their motivations that keeps it palatably fresh, but the exploration and setting will likely be the greatest draw of this fantastic game - to the point where gathering collectibles doesn't feel like the chore that is realistically is. I've completed about 85% of the game according to the ingame stat tracker so with everything done, so you can probably expect about 40 hours of fun to finish fully. Definitely not bad if you get it on a sale.

If you liked the other two TR games from 2013 and 2015, you'll enjoy this one too. If you liked the exploration, platforming and puzzles more than the combat encounters in those games, you'll enjoy this even more, considering there are hardly any gun fights in this game. There have not been many major changes to gameplay here, aside from the much better stealth mechanics, variable difficulties and a larger skill tree. Where this game lacks is in the overall writing of the plot and the boring side missions. The plot feels a bit rushed, especially the ending, which was not a very satisfying conclusion to the trilogy IMO. Some side missions felt a bit pointless, some were interesting, however most of them had flat dialogue. That being said, the game is a very fun 20-25hr ride with loads of side content, challenge tombs etc. The positives far outweigh the negatives here.
